newsitem.title: USA: SBC Comms. to re-route Internet traffic.
newsitem.headline: SBC Comms. to re-route Internet traffic.

text.p: SBC Communications Inc on Tuesday said it has introduced a technology into its five-state region which will siphon off Internet traffic to head off worries about congestion on the U.S. phone network.
The technology, developed by Northern Telecom Ltd recognises and splits off Internet traffic and routes it to a new high speed network. Currently voice and data calls share the same network.
The technology is called Internet/Intranet Transport Service (IITS) and will be marketed under the Southwestern Bell brand name.
"We are enthusiastic about the prospects for this product and the benefits it will bring to our customers," said SBC Chairman Edward Whitacre.

SBC said that initiative would cost less than $100 million. Some regional Bells executives have complained that upgrading their networks to cope with the 150-200 percent annual increase in Internet traffic is unfair because they do not get access charges to connect Internet calls.

The average Internet call is 20.8 minutes, compared with 3.8 minutes for an average phone call. Unlike a network designed for data, local phone networks dedicate a whole line for each call, even if little or no data is traversing it.
SBC is in the process of acquiring Pacific Telesis Group, an acquisition that is expected to be completed by the end of the first quarter.
PacTel's California territory has had the worst problems with Internet congestion.

Executives at SBC said they could make no plans to extend the technology into California until the acquisition was complete, however they acknowledged it would be the area where such a technology would be most useful. -- Nick Louth, New York newsroom 212 859 1610
